subject: social-studies

sections.scope_note: Arizona standards deferred. This crosswalk covers Florida Social Studies (2026) SS.6 codes and IB MYP individuals and societies only. Rows are suggested (Label C). SS.68.AA and SS.68.HE (15 band benchmarks) were omitted from the grade-6 Florida files because they are shared middle-school codes, not grade 6 only, so they are not in these rows.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: criterion B Investigating
MYP individuals and societies: original source material
rows.key_differences: Florida asks for timelines, time-period terms, primary and secondary sources, methods of historical inquiry, historiography, and how history transmits culture. MYP investigating is a criterion title. It does not list those terms.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Place three events on a timeline and say whether one source about them is primary or secondary.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: discrete course example history
MYP individuals and societies: criterion A Knowing and understanding
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies hunter-gatherers, agriculture, river civilizations, Egypt, Mesopotamia, Israelites, and Mesoamerican and South American civilizations. MYP allows a history course. It does not name this list.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Compare one feature of two early river civilizations using a source, and keep the comparison inside the Florida benchmarks rather than adding an IB outcome.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: discrete course example history
MYP global context: orientations in space and time
rows.key_differences: Florida covers Phoenicia, Greece, Rome, Kush, and Axum, including wars, government, and the spread of Latin and Christianity. That sequence is the state grade-6 world history list, not an MYP syllabus. The curriculum page spells the context “orientations in space and time.”
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Choose one classical civilization and one contribution the Florida benchmark names, and explain it with a source.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: discrete course example history
MYP example key concept: global interactions
rows.key_differences: Florida covers India and China, including Hinduism, Buddhism, the Mandate of Heaven, Confucius, the silk roads, the Mongol empire, and Chinese limits on foreign trade. Global interactions is an example key concept, not this content list.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Trace one good or idea that moved along a route named in SS.6.W.4.10 and name the civilizations it connected.

rows.topic_domain: Civics links to ancient Greece and Rome
ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: discrete course example civics
MYP individuals and societies: criterion D Thinking critically
rows.key_differences: Florida asks how Greek and Roman ideas, rule of law, and civic virtue relate to the United States’ constitutional republic. The Florida standard title says “understating”; that is kept in the Florida file and is not an IB term. MYP names civics as a possible course only.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Explain one ancient Greek or Roman political idea and one way the Florida benchmark connects it to the United States.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: discrete course example economics
MYP individuals and societies: criterion A Knowing and understanding
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies scarcity, opportunity cost, supply and demand, barter, traditional and command economies, and trade among named civilizations. Economics is a possible MYP discipline. These concepts are not quoted as MYP objectives.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Pick one early civilization and describe one medium of exchange and one barrier to trade named in the Florida benchmarks.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: discrete course example geography
MYP example key concept: time, place and space
rows.key_differences: Florida requires latitude and longitude, map projections, natural wonders, scale and direction, major bodies of water, and boundaries of ancient civilizations. Geography is a named possible course. The skill list is Florida’s.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use latitude and longitude to locate one ancient civilization and one body of water that affected it.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: example key concept time, place and space
MYP global context: orientations in space and time
rows.key_differences: Florida asks how physical geography shaped ancient civilizations and how to read choropleth or dot-density maps of ancient population. Those map types are not on the public MYP pages.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Explain one physical feature that shaped a river-valley civilization in the Florida list.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: factors that have an impact on individuals, societies and environments
MYP global context: fairness and development
rows.key_differences: Florida covers agriculture and industry, human impact on ancient ecosystems, migration, belief systems, scarcity, transport networks, and famine and natural disasters. The individuals and societies page mentions environmental factors. It does not list these benchmarks.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Show one ancient migration or resource limit on a map and say how it affected a society in the grade-6 list.

ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: criterion C Communicating
MYP individuals and societies: discrete course example geography
rows.key_differences: Florida names the Six Essential Elements of Geography and asks students to compare ancient and current political maps. Those six elements are a Florida sentence, not an MYP objective.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Compare one ancient political boundary with a current map and say what changed.

rows.topic_domain: History of communism - ancient communal systems
ib_framework_elements: MYP individuals and societies: criterion D Thinking critically
rows.key_differences: SS.6.HC.1.1 says: Explain ancient communal systems and the effect on their respective societies. The Florida standard title mentions failures; the benchmark does not. The public MYP pages retrieved do not name communism or communal systems. Criterion D is only a title. This row does not create an IB learning outcome.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Teach the Florida benchmark as a state requirement. Do not rewrite it as an MYP objective.

version_notes: 2026-10-03: Grade 6 FL↔IB crosswalk for MYP, not PYP. Arizona left empty (deferred). Rows are suggested alignments (Label C). Florida IDs are from the grade 6 drafts. IB elements are public MYP framework text or criterion titles from the linked subject brief. No IB learning outcomes and no 1-8 criterion descriptors were invented.
